summary: Still reproduces on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e) and on all 20 measured releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607, no invalid probes; v1.6.2104 shipped 4 days before the report and reproduces. The body is narrower than the measured behavior: each tested integral-constant-expression use rejects a vector or matrix component, not just an array bound - case labels, enumerators, non-type template arguments and [numthreads] each fail with their own diagnostic. Also refused: .x on a static const scalar, matrix ._11/._m00/[0][0], .r, rvalue swizzles, v2[1], v2.x+v2.y. The tested scalar-alias workaround fails too, and constexpr is not a DXC keyword. Unaffected by -HV 2016/2017/2018/2021. FXC 10.1 accepts every tested form including case v2.x and vector<float,v2.y>; clang trunk accepts (10).x - the exact case filed - and rejects the static const ones only under the ordinary C++ non-constexpr rule, accepting them when spelled constexpr uint2. Rejected by two HLSL-specific sites in ExprConstant.cpp (CheckICE blacklist at 9035-9036, IntExprEvaluator::VisitCastExpr at 7749-7750), both dating to the 2016 initial commit; err_hlsl_vla is raised at SemaType.cpp:2142-2146. The only HLSLVectorElementExpr visitor in the constant evaluator is in VectorExprEvaluator, so only vector-result swizzles fold; there is no VisitExtMatrixElementExpr at all. DXC pins this in its own test suite - tools/clang/test/SemaHLSL/const-expr.hlsl:379-382, added 2017-08-29 in 6322c8ca3 (PR #605) - marking it fxc-pass with the comment "It would be desirable to have this supported", so any fix must update that test. Whether to fold component access into a constant expression is a language decision (match FXC, or adopt clang constexpr rules which HLSL cannot spell) and is not pre-empted here.
title: Component swizzling / vector indexing not considered a constant expression
